data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A formal proof checker shares no representation with a human mathematician, yet they can verify the same proof; shared representation is not always necessary for verification.","Two different engines may share tokenizers or architectures, so process-level separation does not guarantee representational separation."],"overturn_conditions":["Demonstration that frozen-module verification catches notation errors the generative module makes would show representational independence despite shared infrastructure.","Proof that all cross-engine pairs also share representational geometry would make the criterion vacuous."],"shared_structure":["Two agents sharing a representational system share its systematic errors.","Freezing parameters prevents adaptation but not inheritance of representational bias.","True independence requires different representational systems, not just different parameters."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001","SRC_003"],"transfer_claims":["The split-brain architecture's failure mode transfers: a frozen module can still misread a notation the same way the generator did.","The perturbation test should be applied at the representation level: feed the checker a notation variant the generator mishandled and check whether the checker also mishandles it."]},"claim":"Even a frozen, separately-trained verification module inside the same engine does not achieve independent verification, because it shares the engine's tokenization, attention patterns, and representational geometry with the generative module; engine separation at the process level is necessary, not merely module separation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the verification module operates on a raw execution trace rather than on the engine's internal representation, the shared representation is bypassed and independence may hold.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If empirical tests show frozen-module errors are uncorrelated with generative-module errors despite shared infrastructure, the representational-inheritance argument is falsified.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If two modules share representational infrastructure, errors that are systematic to that infrastructure (e.g., misreading a notation, misweighting a context window) propagate to both modules. A frozen weight set prevents online updating but does not prevent shared systematic misrepresentation, so the verifier inherits the author's representational blind spots.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
